lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.d: Hosea's word to Israel in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash and Judah's kings: a prophet's marriage to an unfaithful wife pictures the LORD's love for faithless Israel, followed by charges, judgment and a call to return.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences how Hosea's marriage pictures the LORD's relationship with Israel?
ev: Say that Hosea's marriage (chs 1-3) is an acted picture of the LORD and Israel
Outline the book as marriage (1-3), charges and judgment (4-13) and a closing call to return (14)

nodes.d: The LORD tells Hosea to take a wife of whoredoms; their three children are named Jezreel, Loruhamah and Loammi as signs, yet the chapter ends with a promise that Israel will be called sons of the living God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the names of Hosea's three children meant and what hope the LORD adds at the end of chapter 1?
ev: Name the three children and what each name signals
Point out the promise in 1:10-11 that reverses 'not my people'

nodes.t: The LORD pleads and allures his wife
nodes.d: The LORD charges Israel with going after her lovers and forgetting him, announces discipline, then promises to allure her into the wilderness and betroth her to himself for ever in faithfulness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how chapter 2 moves from judgment on Israel to the LORD betrothing her again?
ev: Describe the charge (2:5, 2:8, 2:13) and the discipline (2:6-13)
Describe the promise to betroth Israel for ever (2:19-20) and to say 'Thou art my people' (2:23)

nodes.d: The LORD tells Hosea to love a woman who is an adulteress, as he loves Israel; Hosea buys her and tells her to wait for him, and Israel is said to wait many days before returning to seek the LORD and David their king.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Hosea 3 and say what it shows about the LORD's love for Israel?
ev: Retell what Hosea did and what he said to the woman
Say what the action pictures about Israel in 3:4-5

nodes.t: The LORD's controversy with the land
nodes.d: The LORD charges the people and priests with no truth, mercy or knowledge of God, with violence, idolatry and sexual sin at the high places, and declares that his people are destroyed for lack of knowledge.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say why the LORD has a controversy with the land in Hosea 4?
ev: List the sins named in 4:1-2 and 4:12-14
Explain 4:6 in plain words

nodes.t: Priests, house of Israel and Judah judged
nodes.d: Priests, people and king are warned that judgment is coming; Ephraim and Judah turn to Assyria for healing but cannot be healed, and the LORD says he will withdraw until they acknowledge their offence and seek his face.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Ephraim's help from Assyria fails in Hosea 5 and what the LORD waits for?
ev: Say whom the LORD addresses in 5:1
Explain why turning to the Assyrian could not heal them (5:13)
Say what the LORD waits for in 5:15

nodes.t: Return to the LORD; mercy, not sacrifice
nodes.d: The people speak of returning to the LORD who has torn and will heal, but the LORD answers that their goodness is like morning dew, that he desires mercy and the knowledge of God more than offerings, and that they have transgressed the covenant.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD means in Hosea 6:6 when he says he desires mercy, not sacrifice?
ev: Read the call to return in 6:1-3 and the LORD's reply in 6:4-6
Explain 6:6 in plain words
Notice the reference to transgressing the covenant in 6:7

nodes.d: The LORD would heal Israel but finds falsehood and treachery, from the king and princes down; Ephraim is like a half-baked cake and a silly dove that calls to Egypt and goes to Assyria rather than crying to the LORD with the heart.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD compares Ephraim to a silly dove in Hosea 7?
ev: Describe two pictures used for Ephraim (7:8, 7:11)
Say what Ephraim does instead of turning to the LORD (7:11, 7:14)

nodes.t: Sowing the wind, reaping the whirlwind
nodes.d: The trumpet sounds because Israel transgressed the covenant, set up kings and idols of their own making and the calf of Samaria; they sow the wind and reap the whirlwind, and will return to Egypt.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what it means that Israel sows the wind and reaps the whirlwind?
ev: Name the charges in 8:1, 8:4 and 8:12
Explain the saying in 8:7

nodes.d: Israel is told not to rejoice, since the land will not feed them and they will go into Assyria and Egypt; the LORD recalls finding Israel like grapes in the wilderness before they went to Baalpeor and Gilgal, and Ephraim's fruit is cut off.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how the LORD first found Israel in Hosea 9:10 and what the people did next?
ev: Say where the LORD says Israel will go (9:3, 9:6, 9:17)
Describe the picture of 9:10 and what went wrong

nodes.d: Israel the vine bears fruit for himself and multiplies altars and images; calves and king will be carried off, yet the LORD calls them to sow righteousness and seek him until he rains righteousness on them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the call to sow in righteousness in Hosea 10:12 and what Israel had sown instead?
ev: Explain why Israel is called an empty vine (10:1)
Read the call in 10:12 and say how it contrasts with 10:13

nodes.t: Out of Egypt: the LORD's fatherly love
nodes.d: The LORD remembers calling his son out of Egypt, teaching Ephraim to walk and drawing them with bands of love, yet they turned to Baalim; he declares he will not carry out the fierceness of his anger, for he is God and not man.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how the LORD speaks about Israel as his child in Hosea 11:1-4 and 11:8-9?
ev: Retell 11:1-4 in your own words
Explain what 11:8-9 says about the LORD's heart and character

nodes.d: The LORD has a controversy with Judah and Israel; he recalls Jacob taking his brother's heel, wrestling and finding God at Bethel, then calls Ephraim to turn, since the people trade by deceit and trust in wealth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say which parts of Jacob's life Hosea 12 recalls and why?
ev: Say which events of Jacob's life are recalled (12:3-4, 12:12)
Read the call of 12:6 and the sin of 12:7-8

nodes.d: Ephraim's idol worship brings him to vanish like morning cloud; the LORD alone is God and Saviour from Egypt, yet he will come as a lion and bear, though he also promises to ransom them from the grave and death.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Hosea 13:4 says there is no saviour but the LORD?
ev: Summarise 13:4 and 13:9 in your own words
Describe the judgment pictures of 13:7-8
Point to the ransom promise of 13:14

nodes.t: Return, and the LORD will heal
nodes.d: The book ends with a call to take words and return to the LORD, who promises to heal backsliding, love freely and be like dew so that Israel flourishes, with a closing note that the ways of the LORD are right.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Hosea ends, with what Israel is told to do and what the LORD promises?
ev: Say what Israel is told to say and renounce (14:2-3)
Describe the LORD's promises in 14:4-7
Read the closing line (14:9)

nodes.d: The gospel of Matthew, from the genealogy of Jesus Christ, son of David and son of Abraham (1:1), through the five great discourses, the passion and the resurrection, to the closing commission (28:16-20).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Matthew is about and how it begins and ends?
ev: Describe the movement of the book: birth and preparation (1-4), the Sermon on the Mount (5-7), miracles and mission (8-12), parables of the kingdom (13), teaching on the way to Jerusalem (14-23), the coming kingdom (24-25), the passion and resurrection (26-28)
Name where the book starts and ends

nodes.t: Flight to Egypt and return to Nazareth
nodes.d: Warned in dreams, Joseph takes the child to Egypt away from Herod, who has the children of Bethlehem killed; after Herod dies the family returns and settles in Nazareth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the escape from Herod and where the family finally lived?
ev: Trace the family’s journey: Bethlehem, Egypt, Nazareth
Name the three places where Matthew says a prophecy was fulfilled (2:15, 17-18, 23)

nodes.t: Matthew called and eating with sinners
nodes.d: Jesus calls Matthew the tax collector, eats with publicans and sinners, and answers the Pharisees that the sick need a physician and that he came to call sinners.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jesus ate with publicans and sinners?
ev: Say who Jesus called and where he found him
Explain the “physician” saying

nodes.d: Pharisees object that the disciples pluck grain on the sabbath; Jesus cites David eating the shewbread and the priests in the temple, and says the Son of man is Lord of the sabbath.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Jesus said about David and the sabbath?
ev: Explain the Pharisees’ objection
Say what examples Jesus gave

nodes.d: Paul's letter to the Romans, from the greeting and the gospel theme (1:1-17) to its closing greetings and doxology (16:27).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Romans is about, using 1:16-17?
ev: State the letter's theme from 1:16-17
Describe the movement: sin (1-3), justification (3-5), life in Christ and the Spirit (6-8), Israel (9-11), Christian living (12-16)

nodes.d: Paul answers the question of Israel by pointing to God's sovereign choice, from Isaac and Jacob onward, and his mercy.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Romans 9 says about God's choice and mercy?
ev: Link 9:7 to Genesis 21:12 and 9:12 to Genesis 25:23
Explain 9:15-16

nodes.d: Paul writes to the church at Corinth about divisions, sin in the church, questions they asked him, worship, the resurrection and the collection (1:1-16:24).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short outline of 1 Corinthians and name three problems Paul corrects in the Corinthian church?
ev: Name the main problems Paul addresses: divisions, immorality, lawsuits, marriage, food offered to idols, the Lord's supper, gifts, the resurrection
Say who the letter is addressed to from 1:2

nodes.t: The resurrection body and the victory over death
nodes.d: Paul answers how the dead are raised, with the picture of a seed, contrasts the natural and spiritual body and the first and last Adam, and describes believers being changed at the last trumpet with death swallowed up in victory.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Paul says will happen to the dead in Christ and to the living, using 1 Corinthians 15:42-58?
ev: Explain the seed picture (15:36-38)
Contrast sown and raised in 15:42-44
Explain how believers will be changed (15:51-53)
State the closing exhortation of 15:58

nodes.d: 1 Peter is a letter from the apostle Peter to scattered strangers in Asia Minor, written to encourage them in suffering with the living hope, the example of Christ, holy conduct and humility under God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how 1 Peter encourages believers who suffer?
ev: Say who wrote 1 Peter and to whom
Name the main themes: hope, holiness, suffering and humility

nodes.t: The living stone and the holy priesthood
nodes.d: Peter calls Christ the living stone chosen by God, says believers are built up as a spiritual house and royal priesthood, and says they were once not a people but are now the people of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name three things Peter calls believers in 1 Peter 2:9?
ev: Explain the stone picture in 2:4-8
List the names Peter gives believers in 2:9
Say what 2:10 says changed for them
